To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a model to calculate the energy spectra of the forward-going ejectile, detected with the help of a proton detector, in coincidence with two protons and three protons, in charge-exchange reaction on the 12C target, in terms of pion absorption cross sections.
the multi-proton emission spectra are well explained by the virtual-pion model, and the cross sections are well approximated by the measured absorption cross sections for real pions.

the measured spectra of the ejectile in coincidence with two protons and three protons are reproduced well with the calculated ones, using the measured cross sections of the absorption of real pions in the target nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the multi-nucleon transfer reaction mechanism.
the investigation of the Δ region by charge-exchange reactions in which the ejectile is detected in coincidence with one or more protons.
a study of the multi-proton emission in charge-exchange reaction on the light target nuclei, using the pion absorption as the mechanism of the emission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed forward going protons and tritons are the result of a multi-proton emission process.
the multi-proton emission is due to the absorption of a virtual pion beam in the target.
the (π+, 1p), (π+, 12C), and (π+, n) absorption cross sections are well reproduced by the calculated spectra.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed multi-proton emission in the Δ region in charge exchange reaction can be explained by the virtual pion emission model.
the measured energy spectrum of the ejectile in the forward direction is a direct measure of the (π+, N) absorption cross section, where N is a neutron, proton or a deuteron.
the multi-proton emission in the Δ region in charge exchange reaction is well explained in terms of the Δ resonance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorption of a real pion is a good approximation for the absorption of a virtual pion.
the absorption cross section is the main ingredient for the description of the spectra.

the measured energy spectra of the forward-going ejectile in the (π+, 4p) reaction are consistent with the assumption that the pions are absorbed by the nucleus, which is a necessary condition for the validity of the distorted wave impulse approximation.
